items.title: 68533_Sam Jones oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Amos Milburn's Band' in the context of discussing commercial music groups and venues, but does not describe a personal interaction, collaboration, or direct professional relationship with Amos Milburn himself.

ctx.x: fluence cause trying to figure out what has caused these different intracies. It seems like there is a lot of confusion going on with a lot of people. Like you said, the program directors, the people up there who are programming what they say is jazz and they don't, in your estimation and in mine also, they ain't playing no jazz. But do you think this is possibly some of it; have an influence, this idea of group orientation as opposed to individuals.

Yeah, you see, man, this is the same thing warmed all over again. It's always been ah, ah, ah, those kinds of groups. It's always been. I worked in them, you know. Like, ah, Paul "Hucklebuck" Williams; I played in that band. So, I was around the people Clovers, like the Orioles, the./the, you know, all those different kinds of groups. You know, Amos Milburn's Band you know, all those guys, they don't--
But they have to call themselves jazz right?
